hints: Start from the recursion that produces every subset. Where exactly does it produce the same subset twice?
When two equal values sit at different positions: taking the first and taking the second give the same subset.
Sort the values, so equal ones are adjacent. Then at each level, among a run of equal values, only allow the *first* of the run to be chosen.

'First of the run' means a value equal to the one immediately before it in the sorted list - but only when that predecessor was itself a choice at this same level, not merely earlier in the list. That distinction is the whole rule, and getting it the other way round makes whole subsets disappear.
